title: Ministry of Women and Child Development has issued National Minimum Standards and Protocol in 2024 for setting up creches
body_text:
The Ministry introduced Anganwadi cum Creches (Palna) scheme w.e.f. 01 April 2022, for providing day care creche facilities in safe and secure environment to children (aged 06 months – 06 years) of all mothers irrespective of their employment status along with nutritional support, health and cognitive development of children, growth monitoring, immunization, education etc. Anganwadi centres are the world's largest childcare institutions dedicated for providing essential care and support to children ensuring delivery of care facilities till the last mile.
Palna is a centrally sponsored scheme and implemented with a funding ratio of 60:40 between Centre and State Governments and UTs with legislature except North East & Special Category States where ratio is 90:10. For UTs without legislature, 100% funding will be provided by the Central Government. The requirement of Anganwadi-cum-Crèche Centres (AWCCs) is assessed by the respective States/UTs, and proposals are approved by the Programme Approval Board (PAB) after detailed discussions with the concerned States/UTs. Presently, a total of 4,172 Anganwadi-cum-Crèches (AWCCs) are operational across the country.
Ministry of Women and Child Development has issued National Minimum Standards and Protocol in the year 2024 for setting up creches by care service provider who are required to comply with government rules, laws and regulations related to child protection and safety.
Ministry of Labour and Employment has informed that the provisions of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 have been subsumed under the Code on Social Security, 2020, which came into effect on 21.11.2025. Section 67 of the Code on Social Security, 2020 provides for creche facilities for establishment with 50 or more employees. Under the Code, enforcement in respect of establishments under the State Sphere is the responsibility of the respective State Governments. Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) Organisation under the Ministry of Labour and Employment is the designated enforcement authority for ensuring compliance with maternity benefit provisions in establishments under the Central Sphere.
This information was given by the Minister of State for Women and Child Development Smt. Savitri Thakur in Rajya Sabha in reply to a question.

ministry.name: Ministry of Women and Child Development

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Women and Child Development informed the Rajya Sabha that it issued National Minimum Standards and Protocol in 2024 for setting up creches, mandating compliance with child protection and safety rules. This is linked to the Anganwadi cum Creches (Palna) scheme, launched from 1 April 2022, which currently has 4,172 operational Anganwadi-cum-Crèche Centres (AWCCs) across the country. The Code on Social Security, 2020 (effective 21.11.2025) has subsumed the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, with Section 67 mandating creche facilities in establishments with 50 or more employees.
enrichment.context:
The Palna scheme addresses a long-standing gap in India's childcare infrastructure by providing safe, quality day-care facilities for children aged 6 months to 6 years, regardless of their mothers' employment status, integrating nutrition, health monitoring, immunization, and early cognitive development. Anganwadi centres, under the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) framework, are considered the world's largest childcare network, and Palna builds on this infrastructure with a Centre-State cost-sharing model (60:40 generally, 90:10 for NE/special category states, 100% for UTs without legislature). The 2024 National Minimum Standards and Protocol aim to standardize quality and safety across both government-run and private creche facilities, addressing concerns about unregulated childcare services.

This development also intersects with labour law reforms: the consolidation of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 into the Code on Social Security, 2020 reflects the government's broader labour codification exercise (four labour codes replacing 29 central labour laws) aimed at simplifying and modernizing labour regulations. Section 67's creche mandate for establishments with 50+ employees seeks to support working mothers' workforce participation, a key concern given India's relatively low female labour force participation rate. The enforcement bifurcation between State Sphere and Central Sphere establishments reflects India's federal labour governance structure.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Anganwadi cum Creches (Palna)' scheme is associated with which of the following age groups of children?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release specifies that the Palna scheme provides day-care creche facilities to children aged 6 months to 6 years, irrespective of their mothers' employment status.

prelims_questions.question: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, creche facilities are mandated for establishments employing how many or more workers?
prelims_questions.explanation: Section 67 of the Code on Social Security, 2020 mandates creche facilities for establishments with 50 or more employees, as stated in the release.
